clue.text: Savoury sausages from a Greek island

definitions.meaning: spiced cured sausages from Italy, plural
an island in the Saronic Gulf near Athens, site of a famous sea battle

explanation.surface: A menu note boasting that the cured meats were brought over from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the Italian cured sausage and the name of the Greek island near Piraeus share one spelling.

parts.note: reads as a star architect, but also a small bird that flies, sharing its name with the architect of St Paul's

explanation.surface: Praise for a brilliant, rising architect.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral in London; the same name belongs to a tiny songbird, a literal high-flyer.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Britain's most famous architect is also a small bird, so it is both a building genius and a flyer.

parts.note: a coaster is a small mat put under a drink

explanation.surface: Asking what the design plan is for a drinks coaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a coaster is described as a kind of mat, giving FOR + MAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A layout or plan for how something is arranged is its blueprint.

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman
pent means shut in or confined

explanation.surface: A young woman locked up and drunk, or a life thrown away behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Time or money squandered foolishly has been wasted.

definitions.meaning: fed up and gloomy, a British idiom
literally, food that has been cooked under the grill until it goes brown

explanation.surface: Someone who feels low after a fierce interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom for fed up also literally describes toast or meat browned under a grill.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom for fed up and gloomy is also literally what grilled food becomes, coloured by the heat.

definitions.meaning: describing an aromatic substance that is burnt slowly to give fragrant smoke
as a verb, to enrage or infuriate

explanation.surface: A description of anger that burns slowly beneath the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the noun for the fragrant smouldering stuff; the second is the verb stressed on the second syllable, to enrage.
explanation.definitionFit: Joss sticks smoulder to give scented smoke, and the same word as a verb means to enrage.

clue.text: Sounds as if one can manage something rotten

indicators.note: tells us the letters are chosen to match a spoken phrase

parts.note: to carry on is to keep going or cope

explanation.surface: A claim that someone can cope with something that has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaying flesh of dead animals is rotten meat.

indicators.note: the fighter is put in front of the tirade, facing it

parts.note: the MiG is a Soviet-built fighter jet
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: A wandering Russian soldier confronted with an angry outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who moves from place to place for work is a wanderer, an itinerant.

definitions.meaning: an old adjective meaning fitting or suitable
as a verb, to seize or take for oneself

explanation.surface: An instruction to gather and then seize something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet' is the archaic adjective meaning proper, not the verb; the second sense is the verb stressed differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means suitable and the verb means to seize for one's own use; both are spelt the same.

clue.text: A great work of literature in Latin

definitions.text: A great work of literature in Latin

parts.words: A great work of literature in Latin
parts.note: reads as a classical text, but describes the Latin phrase meaning great work

explanation.surface: A description of a classic book written in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase itself is Latin for 'great work', so it is literally a great work expressed in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase for an artist's or writer's masterpiece translates as 'great work'.

clue.text: Feeble fellow of very little note

parts.note: wee is Scottish for very small
D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A weak man of no importance at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A weakling, especially a skinny one, is a feeble fellow.

clue.text: A column I coated in stucco

indicators.note: the letter I is covered by the stucco, so it sits inside that word

parts.note: stucco is a kind of plaster for walls

explanation.surface: A column the speaker has covered with stucco.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangular column projecting slightly from a wall is a decorative pillar.

parts.note: a lie is an untruthful statement
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A dishonest nation causes its people to become estranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An untruthful' suggests 'an untruthful thing', a lie, so A + LIE + NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling estranged or isolated from a group is disaffection.

clue.text: To a great extent,'tis always thus

parts.note: ever means always
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned remark that something has always been this way, very much so.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means very or extremely, to a great degree.

definitions.meaning: dissolute living and indulgence in vice
squandering money or resources

explanation.surface: Moralising that a life of vice leads to squandered money.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a life of indulgence and the frittering away of money.

clue.text: Discard a controversial EC farming policy

definitions.meaning: to put aside or reject
the European Community scheme paying farmers to leave land uncultivated

explanation.surface: A call to drop a disputed European agricultural rule.
explanation.walkthrough: The European Community scheme paid farmers to leave fields unplanted, and was much criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to put aside or discard, and also names the EU scheme of leaving farmland fallow.

indicators.note: the lad takes the single word into his middle, so it sits inside

parts.note: a boy is a lad
lone means single or solitary

explanation.surface: A boy gulping down one striped boiled sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: A humbug is also a British striped mint sweet, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or empty talk is humbug.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a quire is an old spelling of choir, singers gathered together

explanation.surface: Instructions to recruit a hundred singers for a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIRE is the archaic spelling of choir, still used in church contexts.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to own or obtain something is to get it.

clue.text: French maid takes time to make a hat

indicators.note: the maid takes on the time letter, placed after her

parts.note: bonne is French for a maid

explanation.surface: A French servant spending time making a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A brimless cap tied under the chin is a kind of hat.

definitions.meaning: in reality, in practice
in force, as of a law that applies

explanation.surface: A short phrase saying something really is working.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both in reality and in force, as a rule that applies.

clue.text: No TV channel reflected his inventive genius

indicators.note: a mirror reflection turns the whole run of letters back to front

parts.note: side is old British slang for a television channel

explanation.surface: Lamenting that no television station did justice to an inventor's brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns NOSIDE into EDISON; 'side' is dated British slang for a TV channel ('switch over to the other side').
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison, the American who devised the phonograph and light bulb, was a great inventor.

definitions.meaning: a great multitude or army
a master of ceremonies who presents a show

explanation.surface: A military honours ceremony, with the Military Cross presented.
explanation.walkthrough: MC looks like the Military Cross, matching 'Army awards', but it is the master of ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavenly or earthly army is a multitude, and a compere introduces a show.

clue.text: Starting off by making a display

definitions.meaning: beginning a journey
arranging things to show them

explanation.surface: Beginning a journey by putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both beginning a journey and arranging things for show.

definitions.meaning: to go past or elapse
a small spiny-finned fish of coastal waters

explanation.surface: A request at the table to hand over the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to pass by, and the same letters name a small sea fish.

definitions.meaning: as a verb, moves a worker temporarily to another post
extra helpings of food

explanation.surface: Moving staff while dishing out more helpings.
explanation.definitionFit: To move staff temporarily to another post, and extra helpings at a meal, share this word.

clue.text: Doctor in directors' pocket is subject to attack

indicators.note: the doctor sits inside the directors' word, as if tucked in their pocket

parts.note: a board is a body of directors
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

explanation.surface: A company physician in the board's pocket faces an onslaught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'pocket' adds the picture of a doctor bought by the company, without changing the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail with shells or questions is to attack relentlessly.
